verses.text: My son, listen to the wisdom I'm giving you. Lean in to hear what I've learned.
That way you'll hold on to good judgment, and what you say will show that you know better.
The lips of a woman breaking her marriage vows drip with honey. Her words slide down smoother than oil.
But in the end she's bitter as wormwood and sharp as a blade that cuts both ways.
Her feet go down to death. Her steps head straight for the grave.
She doesn't give the road to life a thought. Her paths are crooked, and she doesn't even realize it.
So now, my sons, listen to me. Don't stray from what I've told you.
Take a route that stays far from her. Don't go anywhere near her front door.
Otherwise you'll hand your honor to other people and give your years to someone cruel.
Strangers will feast on your wealth, and all your hard work will make somebody else's household rich.
At the end you'll groan as your flesh wastes away and your body gives out.
You'll say, “I hated being taught. Deep down I couldn't stand having anybody correct me.
I didn't listen to my teachers. I wouldn't even hear out the people who tried to teach me.
Here I am at the edge of total ruin, right in front of everybody.”
Drink from your own cistern. Enjoy the fresh water flowing from your own well.
Should your springs spill out into the streets and your streams run through the public squares?
Keep that water for yourself. Don't share it with strangers.
May your spring be blessed, and take joy in the wife you married when you were young.
She's a loving doe, a graceful deer. Let her breasts satisfy you always, and let her love always sweep you away.
My son, why let another man's wife sweep you away? Why hold another woman close?
Everything people do is right in front of the LORD. He watches every road they take.
The wicked get caught in the evil they do. Their sin wraps around them like ropes and holds tight.
They'll die for lack of discipline. Their own foolishness will take them way off course.
